speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg; could you tell me how long it has been there and what brought it on? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or redness spreading around the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis

I have noted your history of Crohn's, diabetes, and a recent ant bite, but the one-month progression to an ulcer requires confirmation. REQUEST TEST: Blood smear for Leishmania parasites. REQUEST TEST: PCR for Leishmania DNA from lesion fluid. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photo of the leg lesion to assess for an eschar or raised border.
